payload.headline: Tesla slips to the top of support; valuation still far above cash flow

summary.thesis: Tesla is a grade D business right now: sales are flat, margins are thinner and free cash flow has halved, but the stock still trades near the top of its own 5-year price-to-sales range.
summary.decision: Long-term the call is avoid. On the swing side there is no trade while the price sits between support at 380.15–389.95 and resistance at 393.63–400.51.
summary.act_at: Long-term: revisit near 293.94. Swing: no trade unless the price closes above 417.44 or below 380.15.

payload.happening: Tesla closed at 390.22, down 1.82% on the day. That puts it just above the top of its most-tested support zone (380.15–389.95, 10 touches). The 20-, 50- and 200-day averages (385.36, 374.74, 382.73) are all flat, so the stock is moving sideways in a range. There is no news since the last note, and the next earnings report is on 2027-01-27.
payload.business: Several numbers point to a real change in the business, not just in mood. Sales in the latest quarter were down 0.17% from a year earlier, after growing 15.78% two quarters ago. Operating margin, the share of sales left after running costs, fell to 3.35% from 4.74%. Free cash flow over the last 12 months, the cash left after spending on the business, fell to 3.3B from 6.8B. The filings flag that inventory is up 15% while quarterly sales are up 0%. Unsold cars can force price cuts, which would squeeze the 19.29% gross margin further. These are pressures on demand and margins. The balance sheet is not at risk: Tesla holds 37.5B of net cash (cash minus debt) and 45.4B of total liquidity against 8.0B of debt, so there is no funding problem. The 'tech market in a downtrend' reading from the macro agent affects sentiment, not the business itself.

worth.text: At 390.22, Tesla is valued at about 1542.0B. That is 14.9 times its sales and 429.4 times its earnings per share of 0.91. A cash-flow model (DCF) starts from today's 3.3B of free cash flow and gives 20.23 (bear), 25.02 (base) and 45.34 (bull) per share. Even if growth starts at 30% a year, that model reaches only 44.97. The filings risk note says the price needs about 51% a year growth, while the company delivered 3% a year over 3 years. The second method asks what Tesla is worth if the market keeps paying a price-to-sales multiple in its own 5-year range. That gives 203.8 (low), 293.94 (middle) and 399.81 (high). The gap between the two methods comes from one assumption: whether investors keep paying for future hopes rather than today's cash. The current price-to-sales ratio is at the 78th percentile of its own 5-year history, so the stock sits near the top of the generous method too. (The valuation summary in the data was computed at 397.45, yesterday's price.)
worth.key_assumption: The market keeps valuing Tesla within its own 5-year price-to-sales range rather than on current free cash flow.

bull: Net cash of 37.5B and liquidity of 45.4B mean Tesla can fund its plans through a weak patch without borrowing.
Sales over the last 12 months grew to 103.6B from 95.6B, and analysts' next-year EPS growth is 25%.
The price is above all three of its 20-, 50- and 200-day averages (385.36, 374.74, 382.73), and the 380.15–389.95 support zone has held 10 times.
bear: Free cash flow over the last 12 months halved to 3.3B from 6.8B, and operating margin fell to 3.35% from 4.74%.
Inventory is up 15% while latest-quarter sales are up 0%, which can force price cuts.
The base cash-flow value is 25.02 per share against a 390.22 price, and the price implies about 51% a year growth versus 3% delivered over 3 years.

levels.what: Today's close. It is near the top of the history-based range and far above every cash-flow value.
The top of the own-history price-to-sales range. Above it, even the generous method says the stock is expensive.
The middle of the own-history range. At this level the price would no longer need a top-of-range multiple, so it is worth a fresh look if margins stabilize.

longterm.why: Sales are flat while margins and cash flow are falling, and the stock still trades near the top of its own valuation history. The rules committee call is Reduce, and only grade A or B businesses pass the value rules.

swing.why: The price is boxed between support at 380.15–389.95 and resistance at 393.63–400.51. The room to either edge is smaller than the 16.71 average daily range, so a stop would sit inside normal daily noise. A close above 417.44 or below 380.15 would show a direction.

decision.timing: The 2027-01-27 report comes after the 2027-01-15 options expiry, and options price a 14.8% move by then (implied volatility 45.9 vs realized 61.0). That makes the January report the next real test of margins and cash flow, not the coming weeks.

change_mind: At the 2027-01-27 report, quarterly sales growth moving back toward the 15.78% of two quarters ago, with operating margin back above 4.74%.
Free cash flow over the last 12 months recovering toward 6.8B from 3.3B, together with inventory growth falling back in line with sales.
A daily close above 417.44 (top of resistance) would reopen a swing case, and a close below 380.15 would point toward the 364.02–368.6 support.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still avoid long-term and no swing trade. The 1.82% drop to 390.22 moved the stock onto its 380.15–389.95 support, but free cash flow is still shrinking (3.3B vs 6.8B).
payload.label: Research, not advice.
